name: Representation and Kernel Modifications
text:
# Representation and Kernel Modifications

Also called: Kernel Variants, Primitive Representation Extensions

## Overview
Representation and Kernel Modifications extend the standard [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) primitive definition and rasterization kernel to address limitations in shape flexibility, geometric consistency, and physical realism. While standard 3DGS relies on positive-only, isotropic/anisotropic Gaussian kernels with fixed attributes, this family introduces negative color contributions, voxel-based scaffolding, tangent-plane constrained densification, alternative radial basis functions (RBFs), and spatially varying blur kernels. These methods set themselves apart by altering the fundamental mathematical representation of the radiance field or the optimization dynamics of the primitives, rather than just changing the loss function or camera model.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the differentiable rendering framework of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md), where the scene is represented as a set of 3D Gaussian primitives $\{G_i\}$. Each primitive is typically defined by position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\Sigma_i$ (or rotation/scale), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$. The core rendering pipeline involves projecting these 3D primitives to 2D ellipses and accumulating color via [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md). The modifications in this family do not change the fundamental alpha-compositing equation but alter:
1.  **The Attribute Space:** Allowing negative values (NegGS), deriving attributes from latent features ([Scaffold-GS](#9186-scaffold-gs.md)), or constraining geometric growth ([GeoGaussian](#9187-geogaussian.md)).
2.  **The Kernel Function:** Replacing the Gaussian PDF with other decay functions ([DARBF-Splatting](#9911-darbf-splatting.md)) or applying spatially varying post-rasterization blur (Grid-based Blur).
3.  **The Geometric Interpretation:** Treating Gaussians as oriented surface elements (Gaussian Wrapping) or shell maps (Gaussian Shell Maps).

## Subtopics

### [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Negative Gaussian Splatting](#9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) (NegGS) extends the [primitive representation](#11838-primitive-representation.md) by allowing Gaussian components to have negative color values [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. This modification enables the modeling of high-frequency elements, complex nonlinear structures, and rapid color transitions that are difficult to capture with standard positive-only Gaussians [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. Unlike standard Gaussian Splatting, which requires many components to approximate complex shapes, NegGS uses the subtraction of Gaussian densities (Diff-Gaussians) to achieve greater flexibility in shape representation and color modulation with fewer total primitives [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)
Scaffold-GS is a representation modification for 3D Gaussian Splatting that replaces the direct storage of Gaussian attributes with a voxel-based scaffold [9186-scaffold-gs.md]. It initializes a voxel grid where each voxel holds learnable features, and derives all Gaussian properties (position, covariance, opacity, color) via interpolation and lightweight neural networks [9186-scaffold-gs.md]. This approach decouples the geometric structure from the primitive attributes, addressing initialization sparsity and attribute prediction stability compared to standard 3DGS [9186-scaffold-gs.md].

### [GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)
GeoGaussian is a [training optimization and initialization](#13464-training-optimization-and-initialization.md) strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting that addresses geometric inconsistency and aliasing artifacts by modifying the densification process [9187-geogaussian.md]. It solves the problem of Gaussians growing in arbitrary directions during gradient descent, which leads to jagged surfaces and poor [normal consistency](#3050-normal-consistency.md). It sets itself apart from standard 3DGS by constraining the growth of new primitives to the tangent plane of existing Gaussians and enforcing smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring primitives [9187-geogaussian.md].

### [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)
DARBF-Splatting is a splatting-based 3D reconstruction method that replaces the standard Gaussian kernel with Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs) [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. It solves the limitation of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) being restricted to the exponential family of functions, which often requires many primitives to cover large areas efficiently [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. By using non-exponential kernels like Half-Cosine or [Inverse Multiquadric](#9910-inverse-multiquadric-splatting.md), DARBF-Splatting achieves comparable visual quality with 34% faster training convergence and 15% lower memory usage [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. It sets itself apart from siblings like Negative Gaussian Splatting by focusing on kernel shape generalization rather than attribute sign or neural scaffolding [9911-darbf-splatting.md, 9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md, 9186-scaffold-gs.md].

### [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)
[Grid-based Blur Kernels](#14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md) replace the single, fixed Gaussian kernel of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with a set of learnable, spatially-varying blur kernels indexed by a sharpness prior [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md]. This method solves the problem of modeling spatially-varying defocus blur in radiance fields, which standard 3DGS cannot handle because it assumes a uniform point-spread function across the image plane [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md]. Unlike [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md) which modifies geometric initialization, or [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md) which changes the kernel shape globally, this method retains the Gaussian primitive but allows the rasterization kernel to adapt locally based on estimated scene sharpness [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md].

### Gaussian Shell Maps
Gaussian Shell Maps (GSMs) combine CNN-based generators with 3DGS to recreate virtual humans with sophisticated details such as clothing and accessories [S1]. This approach leverages the generative power of CNNs to produce high-frequency appearance details that are challenging to capture with standard Gaussian attributes alone.

### Gaussian Wrapping
Gaussian Wrapping is a framework that reinterprets 3D Gaussian primitives as oriented probabilistic surface elements representing geometry only within an oriented half-space, allowing derivation of closed-form occupancy, vacancy, and normal fields for watertight mesh extraction [S2]. The method models surface points with asymmetric primitives where the Gaussian models density decay on the outward-facing side, while the inward-facing side is considered fully occupied [S2]. It identifies geometric gaps where the oriented surface assumption is violated and densifies the representation to obtain a watertight shell of oriented primitives [S2]. A learnable oriented normal is introduced at each Gaussian element, and an adapted attenuation formulation enables closed-form expressions for normal and occupancy fields [S2]. A novel consistency loss and dedicated [densification strategy](#6234-densification-strategy.md) enforce Gaussians to wrap the entire surface by closing geometric holes [S2]. The differentiable rasterizer is modified to output depth as an isosurface of the continuous model, and Primal Adaptive Meshing is used for Region-of-Interest meshing at arbitrary resolution [S2].

## Background
The standard [3D Gaussian Splatting method](#4010-gaussian-kernel-volumetric-primitive.md) [Parent](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md) established a fast, differentiable rendering pipeline using 3D Gaussians. However, researchers quickly identified limitations in its representation: the inability to model negative contributions for complex color transitions, the sparsity of initialization, the jaggedness of densified surfaces, and the rigidity of the Gaussian kernel shape.

Negative Gaussian Splatting [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md] and DARBF-Splatting [9911-darbf-splatting.md] address the mathematical constraints of the kernel, allowing for more efficient coverage and complex color fields. Scaffold-GS [9186-scaffold-gs.md] and GeoGaussian [9187-geogaussian.md] focus on the initialization and densification phases to improve geometric stability. Grid-based Blur Kernels [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md] extend the method to handle physical camera effects like defocus. Gaussian Wrapping [S2] and Gaussian Shell Maps [S1] adapt the representation for specific applications like surface reconstruction and human avatars.
